brief: RBC ties a Houthi seizure of Yemen's Mokha port, adding to Houthi control of Hodeidah, to gravely imperiled Bab el-Mandeb shipping and a recent fall in Saudi exports below 2 mb/d, weakening the oil release valve for the ongoing 6-month Iran war. A resumption of full Saudi-Houthi war is the core catalyst behind RBC's high scenario of $121.99/bbl Brent and $118.49/bbl WTI for Q4. Separately, RBC reads Chinese oil demand as recovering: refinery runs above 90% of pre-war levels, crude imports up 19% from June's lows, and product exports up 180 kb/d month over month in August, supporting a view that demand proves structurally resilient post-conflict. European gas prices have hit their highest level since January 2023 on low inventories (EU 67%, Germany 54.8%). RBC doubts a Russian gas reintegration despite an AfD state win in Germany, and expects TTF to stay well bid through winter as Qatari LNG supply stays insufficient to ease the crunch before injection season ends. On gold, RBC reaffirms its year-old bullish call, expecting a $4500-5000/oz range later in 2026 despite Treasury buyback-driven softness, and flags its high scenario as possibly reachable in 2027.
